newsitem.title: USA: Oil drillers, services drop with crude slide.
newsitem.headline: Oil drillers, services drop with crude slide.

text.p: Oil drilling and service shares slid on Wednesday as light sweet crude deliverable May on the New York Mercantile Exchange fell 81 cents a barrel to $19.47, its lowest close since March 4, 1996.
"There are a lot of momentum investors in this sector and that and the fall in crude oil prices are the reasons behind the decline," said Ravi Kamath, analyst at Jefferies & Co.
By 1554 EST, the S&P Oil Drilling Index had fallen 99.54 points, 3.15 percent, to 3,063.24 against a 1.27 percent fall in the wider S&P 500 Index.
The benchmark West Texas Intermediate blend for after Brent crude fell to an eight month low in London trade.

Among the biggest losers, oil services company Schlumberger Ltd was off 3.18 percent to 3-3/8 at 106-3/4, Pride Petroleum shed 5.00 percent, 1 to 19, Falcon Drilling 4.84 percent, or 1-3/4 to 34-3/8, Diamond Offshore was down 3.69 percent, 2-1/2 to 65-1/4, and Global Marine 2.4 percent, 0-1/2 at 20-3/8.
